name: Esketamine
description: Esketamine (Spravato) facts: how it treats depression, the in-clinic dosing schedule, monitoring rules, boxed warnings, side effects, and how to access it.
quick: Esketamine (Spravato) is a nasal spray for treatment-resistant depression and for depression with suicidal thoughts. It is a form of ketamine, given only in certified clinics where patients are monitored for at least two hours. It is a Schedule III controlled substance and is never dispensed to take home.
facts: Treatment-resistant depression (with an oral antidepressant or alone); major depression with suicidal thoughts or actions
At least 2 hours after each dose

blocks.p: Esketamine is approved for adults with treatment-resistant depression, either with an oral antidepressant or, since January 2025, on its own, and with an oral antidepressant for major depression with acute suicidal thoughts or behavior.[[1]]
It is the S-form of ketamine. It works on the glutamate system rather than serotonin, which may explain why it can help people for whom standard antidepressants failed.
Spravato is self-administered under the direct supervision of a clinician at a certified treatment center. The schedule below comes from the label and is not personal dosing advice.[[1]]

Schedule
Dose
rows: 56 mg on day 1, then 56 or 84 mg

blocks.p: Patients must not drive or operate machinery until the next day after a restful sleep, and need someone to take them home.

sections.q: What are the risks and side effects of esketamine?

boxed.title: FDA boxed warnings
items: Sedation, dissociation, and breathing depression; patients must be monitored for at least 2 hours after each dose.
Increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviors in children, teens, and young adults taking antidepressants.

blocks.p: **Common side effects** include dissociation, dizziness, nausea, sedation, spinning sensation, numbness, anxiety, raised blood pressure, vomiting, and feeling drunk.[[1]]
**Who should not use it:** people with aneurysms or arteriovenous malformations, or a history of bleeding in the brain, because it raises blood pressure.[[1]]

sections.q: What happens if someone gets too much esketamine?

blocks.p: Because it is only given under supervision in measured doses, overdose is rare. Excess effects would include heavy sedation, dissociation, and high blood pressure.[[1]]

emergency.title: If someone may have overdosed
items: Call 911 if the person is unresponsive, breathing slowly, having a seizure, very hot, or violently agitated.
Place an unresponsive person on their side so they do not choke if they vomit.
Keep them away from roads, water, and heights. People on dissociatives often cannot feel pain or judge danger.
If opioids could be involved, give naloxone. It will not harm the person.

sections.q: What happens when esketamine treatment stops?

blocks.p: No withdrawal syndrome was seen in trials. Stopping maintenance treatment raises the risk of depression returning; trials showed relapse was more likely in patients who stopped than in those who continued.[[1]]

sections.q: How do you get esketamine legally in the US?

blocks.p: In the United States, esketamine is a Schedule III controlled substance. The only legal way to get it is with a prescription from a clinician registered with the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), filled by a licensed pharmacy. Depending on state law, that can be a physician, nurse practitioner, or physician assistant.[[2]]

ul: **Refills:** a Schedule III prescription can be refilled up to five times within six months of the date it was written. After that, a new prescription is needed.[[3]]

**Telehealth:** federal flexibilities let DEA-registered clinicians prescribe Schedule II to V medicines after a telemedicine visit, without a prior in-person exam, through December 31, 2026. A permanent DEA rule was under final review in late 2026. State rules can be stricter.[[4]]
**Monitoring:** prescribers and pharmacists in most states check a prescription drug monitoring program, a database of controlled-substance prescriptions, before prescribing or dispensing.

**Pharmacies:** a legitimate pharmacy always requires a valid prescription, has a licensed pharmacist available, and is licensed in the state it ships to. The FDA's BeSafeRx tool and the NABP's safe pharmacy list help confirm a pharmacy is real.[[5]][[6]]
**Restricted program (REMS):** Spravato is only dispensed to certified healthcare settings, and patients must be enrolled. Pharmacies do not give it to patients to take home.
**Cost:** most insurers, including Medicare and many Medicaid programs, cover Spravato with prior authorization.

blocks.p: **Traveling:** keep the medicine in its original pharmacy container and carry a copy of the prescription. Check the rules of the destination country before travel, because many countries restrict controlled medicines or require a permit.

No. Spravato cannot be ordered online or delivered to your home. A clinician can evaluate you by telehealth, but every dose must be taken at a certified treatment center under supervision. The manufacturer's website lists certified centers.[[1]]
Any website offering esketamine for home use is not legitimate.

Is Spravato the same as ketamine?
It is the S-form of ketamine, given as a nasal spray. Ketamine infusions for depression are off-label; Spravato is FDA-approved.
Yes. Since January 2025, it is approved without an oral antidepressant for treatment-resistant depression.
